scenario_provenance.archetype_label: Multi-focus on Practices 1 & 2 (formulate questions; collect/represent data)
validity_rules: Unit 1 random-sampling methods only: SRS, stratified, cluster, systematic
non-random convenience and voluntary-response plans must be identified as non-random
stratified samples units within every stratum; cluster samples all units in selected clusters

sources.note: the item stem's verb must match the scored demand

prompt: A researcher wants to study whether the delivery arrived by the promised date among orders placed with an online store last month. Sampling plan: The researcher chooses a random starting position, 4, in a numbered export of all order IDs and then selects that entry and every 8th entry after it. Which choice best describes the sampling method?

options.text: Systematic random sample, because a random start is followed by a fixed interval.
Cluster sample, because the population is divided into groups such as shipping region before the sample is chosen.

misconception_source.label: Confused stratified sampling with cluster sampling

sources.note: CED vocabulary distinguishes SRS, stratified, cluster, and systematic sampling; cluster samples all units within selected clusters, while stratified samples within every stratum

options.text: Convenience sample, because the randomly selected units are the ones the researcher contacts.

misconception_source.label: Called a convenience or voluntary-response sample random

sources.note: 2025 CR Report Q2 flags sampling-method/bias vocabulary errors and incomplete random-sampling procedures; convenience and voluntary response are non-random biased methods

options.text: SRS, because the researcher uses a random starting point from a list.

misconception_source.label: Conflated systematic random sampling with SRS

sources.note: CED vocabulary distinguishes systematic random sampling from SRS as separate random-sampling methods
